metadata.site_name: Loch an Eilein Farmstead / Rothiemurchus Estate Outskirts, Aviemore

properties.description: High-angle oblique aerial perspective looking southwest at 242.5 degrees with a -23.9 degree down-pitch over undulating Highland pasture and ancient Caledonian pinewood fringes.

properties.bedrock: Neoproterozoic Dalradian Supergroup metasediments and late-Caledonian Cairngorm granite intrusions
properties.superficial_deposits: Glacial hummocky till, fluvioglacial sand, and gravel outwash terraces
properties.topsoil: Acidic podzols and peaty gleys under improved pasture

properties.surface_material: Compacted crushed granite gravel, graded earth farm access tracks, and exposed sandy dirt paths crossing rough turf
properties.slope_gradient: Gentle 3-5 degree northwesterly decline toward the River Spey floodplain

properties.canopy_dominant: Pinus sylvestris var. scotica (Scots Pine), Betula pendula (Silver Birch), and Alnus glutinosa along damp hollows
properties.ground_cover: Agrostis-Festuca improved grass swards, Calluna vulgaris patches, and field rushes (Juncus effusus)
properties.boundaries: Post-and-wire livestock fencing, weathered timber gates, and drystone clearance dyke remnants

structures.name: Main Agricultural Shed & Steading
structures.materials: Corrugated fiber cement and profile steel gabled roofing, timber framing, and low Scottish granite rubble plinth

structures.name: Traditional Whitewashed Farmhouse & Annexes
structures.materials: Harl-rendered granite masonry, lime whitewash, Scottish slate roofs with pitched dormers, and stone chimney stacks

structures.name: Ancillary Outbuildings
structures.materials: Corrugated iron roofs with weathered orange-brown rust oxidation, timber cladding

properties.elements: Highland livestock grazing in distant paddocks, agricultural machinery tracks, light farm traffic, and gentle wind-rustle through pine canopy
